segments.text: Good morning.
Day one.
Yesterday you were getting through Day Xero an hour at a time.
This morning you woke up with a whole day behind you.
Nobody can take that day back.
However the night went, it's okay.
Maybe you slept well.
Maybe you were awake at three, staring at the ceiling.
Maybe the first thing you thought of when you opened your eyes was a cigarette.
All of that is normal on a first morning, and none of it means anything has gone wrong.
Let me tell you what's happening, because it helps to know.
All through the prep week, you watched the gap.
That restless, slightly empty feeling that showed up between one and the next.
Each time, you closed it, and it opened again.
Since yesterday, nothing has closed it.
So these first days, it's loud.
That isn't the quit going badly.
That's what it sounds like when the gap is on its way out.
The first few days are usually the hardest.
For most people, withdrawal eases over the next few weeks.
Feeling restless, irritable, low, foggy or hungrier than usual is common right now.
It's temporary.
It's a sign your body is adjusting.
So today, I'm not going to ask much of you.
Today is about the basics.
Here's something worth knowing this week.
Being hungry, thirsty or tired can feel a lot like a craving.
The same restlessness.
The same sense that something's missing.
So before you decide a feeling is a craving, check the basics first.
Let's try it now.
Take one breath, in a way that feels comfortable for you.
Now notice your body.
On your first prep day, you asked where you felt the gap.
Ask again.
Your chest, your throat, your hands, your stomach.
Whatever you find, you don't have to fix it.
Just let it be there for a moment.
Now three quick questions.
When did I last eat?
When did I last drink some water?
How did I sleep?
If one of those answers is "a while ago," start there.
Eat something.
Drink a glass of water.
And if what's left afterwards is a craving, you know what to do with a craving.
You notice it, you name it, you breathe, and you let it pass.
So, today.
Three proper meals.
Water close by, because a glass of water gives your hands and your mouth something to do while a wave passes.
And something easy to reach for between meals.
It's common to feel hungrier, and some people put on a little weight after stopping.
That's normal.
Regular meals, water and some movement can help.
This isn't the moment for a strict diet.
One more thing.
Smoking makes your body clear caffeine faster.
So after you stop, your usual coffee or tea can hit harder, and keep you awake.
A smaller cup, earlier in the day, can help.
In a moment, you'll do a quick check-in and choose what you'll reach for when you're hungry.
And every time a craving passes today, log it.
Each one counts.
You've done a whole day.
Today you do the basics, and let the day carry you.
I'll see you tomorrow.
